implementation_notes: The C++ form is the switch-over-enum plus the parallel hierarchy: adding an operation kind requires a new enumerator, a new case in every switch, a new virtual in every class that must support it, and a new entry in every factory. The fix is to invert the dispatch — a map from enumerator to handler, or the visitor pattern — so adding a case is adding one entry. `std::variant` plus `std::visit` gives the same benefit with compile-time exhaustiveness, which is the property the switch was supposed to have.
idiom_name: one change touching every subclass and every switch over an enum
pitfalls: A `switch` over an enum with no `default` gives a compiler warning per missing case, which is the cheapest guard; adding `default:` removes it and restores the scatter.
Adding a pure virtual method to a base class forces every subclass to change — that is shotgun surgery by design of the hierarchy, and the fix is a non-virtual interface or a default implementation.
Overloaded operators implemented in every derived type are the same shape with more syntax.
